title: background messageBus injects sender.tab.id into payload BEFORE the registry zod parse — schemas without a top-level tabId field silently strip it
trigger: A background handler needs the sender's tabId (e.g. to sendTabMessage back to the originating tab) and reads it from request.payload
principle: messageBus.handleMessage copies sender.tab.id into request.payload, then bus.on() wraps the handler with MESSAGE_REGISTRY[type].schema — zod's default strip drops every key the schema doesn't declare, including the injected tabId/frameId. Any content-script-initiated message that needs tab identity MUST declare `tabId: z.number().int().optional()` (and frameId) at the payload top level; reading request.payload.tabId without declaring it always yields undefined. When it matters for routing, fail closed: a missing tabId on a stream-source request is a no-source error, not a silent default.

cases.context: condensed-audio START handler built `{...input.source, tabId: request.payload.tabId}` — record saved with tabId undefined → SESSION_START could never reach the tab → every record failed 'no-source'. Caught by e2e IDB dump, invisible in unit tests.
cases.bad: source = { ...input.source, tabId: (request.payload as {tabId?: number}).tabId } // zod already stripped it
cases.good: schema: tabId: z.number().int().optional() — then input.tabId survives safeParse

applyFor: new message types handled in background that need sender tab context
